authority.map_identity: verified GameMapID↔ResourceMapID binding or exact official map_desc.map_name only; manual labels are display-only; a filename display hint may never suppress the verified-binding tier
authority.map_geometry: Official Map/Common Map/MapNN/map.nif world geometry; standard Gamebryo AV layout plus signature-gated QQSpeed 20.2.5.23 AV-tail reader; file-native transforms only, no replay fit
authority.drift: replay native action-object Drift table: newer marker-linked layout or older unmarked Drift+adjacent native-effect pair; Shift diagnostic-only; empty Drift requires marker
authority.speed_effects: replay native action-object speed-effect table; code1 Nitro, code2001 small-boost class, code2003 map propulsion effect
authority.actions: replay-native Action Event Table (replay_native_action_event): code8 air boost, code9 landing boost, code19 WCW marker, code24 CW/WCW/CWW common marker, code25 grouped with a code24 = CW, remaining code24 = CWW (decisions/0005)
authority.combo_actions: production CW/WCW/CWW come from the replay-native action event table; the timing-based sequence detector is a diagnostic/disagreement layer only and is never a fallback
authority.driving_sections: derived geometry-topology sections in official map world XY; native Drift/actions are read-only annotations and never mutate section boundaries; never authoritative map identity or ideal line
authority.driving_episodes: DERIVED, non-authoritative Driving Analysis v2. Native actions define the driving-event facts; geometry is used only for position, distance, route difference and section measurement. One episode per logical native Drift action. Native episodes and per-lap metrics are map-independent; only spatial sections / same-map A-B require an authoritative map identity
authority.native_action_semantic_alignment: the action event table may only publish game-facing counts when its anchor codes (2/8/9/18/19/20/24) land on the code2001 effect-table interval starts. Replays that fail the gate are replay variants: raw evidence is published, game-facing counts are withheld (fail closed)
authority.product_statistics: a primary (game-facing) number is only published where the native evidence closes against the gold replays; everything else is published as raw native evidence with an explicit unresolved status and is never renamed into a game-facing label
authority.ab_section_alignment: same-course section anchors only; monotonic gap-tolerant DP in official world XY; descriptive/non-authoritative; unmatched sections stay unmatched
authority.ab_continuous_alignment: within a matched section pair only: monotonic world-XY correspondence establishes a shared spatial overlap window; time/speed/route differences are computed at matched observed positions; no canonical/reference/ideal line
authority.training_analysis: DERIVED, non-authoritative Training Analysis v1.1. Measurement only: no score, no grade, no coaching. Both sides of a comparison are read through ONE shared spatial correspondence built from the two REAL driven trajectories in official world XY - monotonic, order-preserving, heading-compatible, bounded and fail-closed, with time deliberately excluded from its cost - which yields ONE shared progress and ONE shared boundary set, so both sides measure the SAME comparison windows instead of each sectioning its own course. There is exactly ONE delta contract, delta = subject - baseline, so a positive time delta is always time lost by the subject; top_loss_sections holds only delta > 0 and top_gain_sections only delta < 0. Every comparison publishes total_delta = matched_delta + unmatched_delta + non_comparison_delta + residual with a tolerance derived from the measured sample interval and the number of non-comparison boundaries. Same-map A/B requires the SAME authoritative ResourceMapID and is otherwise refused; an out-of-tolerance residual or too little shared coverage is reported degraded rather than smoothed
authority.telemetry_cache: qpf_v1 is a source-SHA + extractor-contract validated transport cache only; it does not add or change semantic authority
authority.native_action_cache: native_action_cache_v1 stores raw replay-native action-object tables (Drift candidates, intervals, records, the adjacent speed-effect tables and their exact status) plus the exact raw tail window they were scanned from. It stores no semantic labels: Nitro / small-boost context / combo / unknown stay re-derived from telemetry rows. Validity binds source replay SHA256+size and the native-action scanner contract only; physical cache facts are audit metadata, and the two caches have independent lifecycles

pending.dynamic_map_scene_geometry: exact moving/animated scene geometry driver remains unresolved; native code2003 propulsion effect is validated independently
pending.small_boost_settlement_parity: code2001 raw vs the game-reported normal small-boost count is unresolved (Gold B: 46 raw vs 39 reported actions, 7 intervals unexplained). Raw/anchored/unresolved are published and no game-facing number is invented
pending.nitro_settlement_parity: game nitro = native code1 interval count + 1 in both gold replays; no native activation marker was found, so the raw interval count is published with parity unresolved
pending.high_resolution_section_ab_detail: optional future backend window endpoint can replace telemetry preview resolution after shared-spatial-gate semantics are validated
pending.telemetry_profile_followup: Use v3.7 pipeline_profile.json on real replays before optimizing any remaining native action-table scans.
pending.duplicate_source_sha_hashing: One replay analysis still incurs an additional SHA256 read inside the MapCatalog Resolve child process even though the orchestrator already owns ReplayReadContext SHA256. This is a small redundant SAV read; pass the precomputed SHA into Resolve if profiling shows it matters.
pending.frontend_request_serialization: The local PowerShell TCP frontend still handles one HTTP request at a time; a long replay analysis request can temporarily block unrelated UI requests. This is acceptable for the current single-user pre-release workflow but is the main remaining responsiveness refactor if concurrent/background analysis is later required.

frontend_contracts.daily_use_statistics: the primary view shows logical/game-facing semantics (drift logical, air, landing, CW/WCW/CWW); raw code2001 / code1 counts are labelled as raw native evidence with their parity status and live in the diagnostics panel. The label 漂移小喷 was removed because raw code2001 is not a normal small-boost count
frontend_contracts.driving_v2_ui: map-first local inspector: route hover/click selects the observed spatial section, the inspector shows entry/min/exit speed, drift duration, native combo facts, boost latency and route distance; when a counterpart is selected it shows side-by-side observed section facts without relabelling independently cut section duration as Training time loss.
frontend_contracts.continuous_ab_v2: matched sections from DP v2 are compared through monotonic world-XY correspondence; leading/trailing boundary mismatch is trimmed into a common spatial overlap window, route/speed/time differences are descriptive, unmatched sections stay unmatched, and no standard/reference line is created
frontend_contracts.training_analysis_v1: time-loss/gain windows are promoted to compact map navigation; loss and gain stay separate, delta is subject - baseline, and the detailed shared-window/reconciliation/raw evidence remains available in Advanced diagnostics. The normal workspace is intentionally sparse and local-first rather than a telemetry dashboard.
frontend_contracts.product_workspace_v1: map-centric workspace: the replay list is a ReplayCatalog-backed entity list (derived *_training/comparison JSON never creates replay cards); the map is the primary navigator; hovering a real driven section opens a local inspector, clicking locks it; the default surface shows only lap/time-loss/speed/drift/action facts needed for local analysis, while raw native evidence and legacy section tables stay behind Advanced diagnostics.
frontend_contracts.product_workspace_v2: default current lap = lap 1; when a different replay is explicitly selected, comparison lap defaults to the same lap number if present (no fastest-lap fallback); default UI segmentation is Drift-derived only and merges adjacent replay-native logical Drift episodes when gap < 0.15 s; recovery ownership is code2001-small-boost-only with sustained-air hard cut: standard Nitro/code1, map propulsion and unknown effects never extend a Drift segment, a sustained native contact_state=0 interval (>=100ms) hard-cuts an owned automatic recovery at take-off; and a segment with no eligible post-Drift small-boost ends at native Drift end; a segment assigned to lap N remains visible through its native segment end even when it crosses into lap N+1; comparison may use same authoritative Resource/Game identity or exact same displayed map name even when the official basemap is unresolved; route modes are all-route (display only), Drift-only, and Drift-start-to-native-recovery-end. UI identity/result semantics are separated: A/current is always blue, B/reference is always orange; performance uses red=slower, green=faster, gray=exact-tie/unavailable, and primary time deltas are rendered as explicit 快/慢/持平 text rather than signed +/- values. Native-corner comparison metrics are own-side measurements: exit speed is the fastest production-telemetry speed from final native Drift end through that side own recovery metric end, and recovery distance is measured on that same own-side interval; neither is clipped by the shared A/B spatial boundary. Strict segment ownership remains code2001-only. When a stream cannot observe native speed-effect state (or a network-low-frequency shadow carries no small-boost/nitro evidence), the metric layer alone may use the game-defined 0.25 s single-small-boost lifetime as a minimum tail; this fallback never extends the drawn segment or comparison window. Primary paired-corner time is a core-efficiency window: it keeps the earlier mapped Drift start but stops at the earlier mapped natural recovery end, so a longer single/double-spray tail cannot enlarge the main time delta. Own-side exit speed, recovery distance and total distance still use each replay's complete natural recovery metric window. Paired recovery comparison publishes three related results: core time stops at the earlier mapped natural recovery end; final net time uses the same start and extends to the later mapped natural recovery end, already bounded by each segment's sustained-air/next-Drift hard cuts; recovery strategy gain is core_delta - final_delta (positive means A/current gains time in the extra recovery span). The map marker/hero shows final net result, while the inspector also exposes core and recovery decomposition.
frontend_contracts.product_workspace_v3: viewport-first layout: the Current Segment inspector is an expanded-by-default draggable/collapsible overlay constrained inside the map; the ReplayCatalog list can collapse into a narrow rail; the map viewport height is derived from the live browser viewport and current map top so the map frame does not extend below the available page merely because of a fixed/min-height rule. These are visual-only controls and never change segment boundaries, comparison windows or analysis authority.
frontend_contracts.first_run_setup: On a clean install the only required user configuration is a valid QQ Speed game directory. Missing MapCatalog/game-resource binding data is initialized in the background; Add Replay remains disabled and the analysis endpoint fails closed until initialization is ready. Existing ready catalogs are never rebuilt implicitly.

decoded_native_action_event_table.decoder: native_action_event_table_v1 decodes a replay-native action event table (u32 count, then count * { u32 time_ms; u32 action_code; u32 reserved }) located structurally: the table ends where the fixed 374-byte SAV trailer begins, and the count is the unique self-consistent fixed point, which resolves in 12/12 archived replays. Action codes are preserved verbatim and are NOT whitelisted (observed: 2,8,9,13,18,19,20,21,22,23,24,25,40,41,43,44,45).
decoded_native_action_event_table.production_semantics: code8 = air boost; code9 = landing boost; code19 = WCW marker; code24 = CW/WCW/CWW common marker; code25 grouped with a code24 (<= 500 ms, no intervening code24/code19 record) = CW; remaining code24 = CWW. Production authority since decisions/0005.
decoded_native_action_event_table.code25_note: raw code25 count is NOT the CW count: code25 also occurs standalone. Gold B has 10 raw code25 events of which 5 pair with a code24 (=CW) and 5 do not.
decoded_native_action_event_table.variant_gate: two archived replays (雪境裂渊-20260924-223202 and 风林火山-20260924-224701, both from the same 2026-09-24 recording session) fail the code2001 alignment gate completely (0/40, 0/45) and a constant time-base offset does not recover the relation (best 4/45 @ +985 ms, 3/40 @ -1150 ms). They are treated as replay variants: raw evidence is published, game-facing counts are withheld.
